findings.issue: PRODUCTION issue, out of scope and already on the backlog (carried over from round 1). Any ApiError with status < 500 makes checkout use a new Idempotency-Key on the next try. That includes the ambiguous 408, 409 and 429 replies, where the first request may already have been processed, so a retry could create a second order or charge.
findings.fix: Track it on the backlog. Keep the same key for 408, 409 (except known business rejections such as OUT_OF_STOCK or PAYMENT_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE) and 429, and add tests for those statuses.

findings.issue: The hostile-input table proves the parser cases that matter (TAB, LF and CR inside the path), but it has no case documenting that Unicode look-alikes are harmless. A future 'tightening' could otherwise be added without a reason, or a regression could go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Optional: add cases showing that '/\uFF0Fevil.example' and '/\u2028/evil.example' stay same-origin paths. Also add a short comment that the WHATWG URL parser removes only ASCII TAB, LF and CR inside a URL (plus leading or trailing C0 characters and spaces, which the startsWith('/') check already blocks), and that non-ASCII characters in a path are percent-encoded, never turned into a host.

summary: Both round-1 test findings are fixed. Every AuthCallbackPage navigation is now checked against the exact text with toBe, so the hostile stored values ('//evil.example/x', String.raw '/\evil.example', '%2F%2Fevil.example', '/\t/evil.example', 'https:', 'javascript:', '') would now fail if safeNext were removed. Each case also checks that the stored key is consumed. The new redirect.test.ts covers safeNext directly, plus the sanitise-on-write and re-sanitise-and-consume-on-read behaviour of rememberPostLoginRedirect and takePostLoginRedirect, which closes the gap left by mocking lib/redirect in the button test. The production fix in apps/product-catalog/src/lib/redirect.ts is correct and complete. Inside a URL, the WHATWG parser removes only ASCII TAB, LF and CR, so the new check that rejects any control character (/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F]/) closes the '/\t/host' bypass and its variants. Leading C0 characters or spaces are already blocked by the startsWith('/') check, and the parser already treats backslash as a slash, which the existing '/\' check handles. Unicode look-alikes (fullwidth solidus U+FF0F, division slash U+2215, U+2028) are not folded into '/' by the URL parser, and IDNA processing applies only to a host component, which a single-slash path does not have. So they stay same-origin paths and need no change. The check runs after the prefix checks and can only make safeNext stricter, so it adds no new risk. The CEO's low-impact assessment agrees with my reading: consumers navigate through react-router, where a cross-origin pushState throws instead of redirecting. The fail-before/pass-after run and the forge-verify pass at 305d540 are recorded. The other delta changes (act() wrapping, show-before-hide for wallet and membership, a renamed key test, removal of unused helpers, the register line) add no security surface. There are no secrets or real PII in fixtures and no new dependencies. Approve. The only remaining item is the backlog-tracked Idempotency-Key status rule in production.
